headline: High risk: Cursor can feed untrusted workspace content into n8n workflows, creating dangerous default-path prompt injection and cascading action errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and uses MCP; n8n workflows can ingest arbitrary file/API inputs and execute downstream nodes. That creates a default pathway where Cursor-produced or user-supplied content can be treated as instructions by n8n. The pair’s shared filesystem and broad egress make this more than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF Cursor output is copied into an n8n workflow node without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF n8n AI Agent or Code nodes parse Cursor-authored text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of editor output into workflows.
Add a provenance/allowlist step before any n8n AI Agent node.
Use a separate workspace directory for untrusted content.
Require manual review before executing workflow nodes that consume Cursor output.
requires-engineering: add content-signing or metadata tagging between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and can egress broadly to model providers and MCP servers; n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and can send it to many integrations. In default use, sensitive workspace data can flow from Cursor into n8n and then onward to third-party services. The blast radius is multiple work products, not just one file.
conditions: IF a workflow imports files or text from Cursor into n8n, those contents may be replicated across integrations.
IF n8n nodes forward workflow payloads to external APIs, data can leave the original workspace.
mitigations: Restrict n8n credentials to least-privilege integrations.
Redact secrets before handing Cursor output to n8n.
Use a staging workflow with dummy data first.
Turn off broad model-provider egress where possible.
requires-engineering: implement field-level data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shell commands. Cursor also modifies git state, while n8n can run Execute Command on the server. If they target the same repo or directory, concurrent writes and git operations can corrupt state or overwrite each other. The profiles show shared-state via local filesystem/server systems, so this is a default-path conflict.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory, write conflicts can occur.
IF n8n Execute Command touches files that Cursor is editing, git or filesystem state may diverge.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the repo.
Avoid concurrent git operations.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code, edits, and shell commands; n8n’s AI Agent node and workflow nodes can act on those outputs. If n8n treats Cursor output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious suggestion can cascade into automated actions, commits, or external API calls. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF n8n workflow steps consume Cursor-generated text without validation, errors can propagate.
IF the workflow triggers external side effects from that text, the blast radius becomes operational.
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before side-effecting nodes.
Require schema validation on Cursor-produced outputs.
Limit workflows to read-only actions during testing.
Log and diff all generated instructions before execution.
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between Cursor and n8n.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while n8n processes whatever the workflow touches and stores credentials on its server. If regulated or personal data is routed from Cursor into n8n workflows, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the two systems. The profiles do not prove a specific regime, so this is a compliance-risk pathway rather than a confirmed violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in Cursor buffers or files and then enters n8n workflows, compliance obligations may change.
IF n8n credentials or logs retain that data longer than the source policy, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workflows.
Review n8n retention settings before use.
Separate credentials by environment.
Mask personal data before workflow ingestion.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls end-to-end.
